dedupe_keys.name: hvac retrofit of a university data centre room in taiwan 2024

description: This design and retrofit case follows the replacement and reconfiguration of the air-conditioning system of a university data-centre room in Taiwan, with the aim of improving energy performance and the resilience of cooling. The researchers measured temperatures in the room before and after the work, built a computational fluid dynamics model validated against the measurements with an overall error below 6 per cent, and used both to compare the thermal environment of the old and new systems. They report that the retrofit improved energy efficiency by 48.71 per cent, lowered the average room temperature by 3.2 degrees Celsius, strengthened the resilience of the HVAC system and cut carbon dioxide emissions by up to 4,341 kg per month. The study was carried out at the National Chin-Yi University of Technology in Taichung and published in the Journal of Building Engineering in 2024; the same team published a companion study on independent row-based cooling retrofits. Coverage: one university data-centre room, before and after the retrofit. Format and access: journal article behind the Elsevier paywall; no open data were found. Caveats: a single small facility; resilience is discussed qualitatively; the exact room and equipment are only described in the paywalled article. Simulation uses: hazard exposure of IT rooms to cooling loss and heat, retrofit design for small data centres, and validated CFD settings for thermal digital twins. Related records: the Turkish air-cooled data-centre retrofit is a similar case with open data, and AlphaDataCenterCooling models a whole cooling plant.
